The lights of the city provided a dramatic backdrop for a clash of philosophies as New York City FC hosted D.C. United in a highly anticipated MLS fixture. With both teams looking to assert their dominance in the conference standings, the match promised intensity and high-stakes football from the opening whistle. Munteanu Breaks the Deadlock On May 3rd, 2026 , the atmosphere was electric as the referee signaled the start of a match defined by tactical discipline and clinical finishing. The early exchanges were characterized by a physical edge, with both sides testing the referee's patience in the middle of the park. Keisuke Kurokawa picked up the game's first yellow card in the 26th minute, a sign of the tightening tension. Just three minutes later, the breakthrough arrived for the visitors. Louis Munteanu found space in the final third and struck a precise effort to put DC United ahead, shifting the momentum firmly in their favor. The opening goal forced the hosts into an early tactical reshuffle, as Aiden O’Neill was withdrawn in the 36th minute to make way for Andres Perea . Despite the change, NYCFC struggled to find a rhythmic response before the break. As the first half drew to a close, the temperature on the pitch continued to rise, resulting in a yellow card for Silvan Hefti deep into stoppage time as the visitors took a narrow lead into the dressing rooms. Tactical Battles and Penalty Drama The second half began with both managers looking to their benches to influence the flow of the match . DC United introduced Aaron Herrera and Nikola Markovic on the hour mark to solidify their shape, while the hosts responded shortly after by bringing on Keaton Parks and Hannes Wolf . Despite the fresh legs for the New York side, the visitors remained the more clinical outfit. The pressure eventually boiled over in the 70th minute when Peglow was cautioned for a mistimed challenge. The defining moment of the contest arrived in the 75th minute when the referee pointed to the spot following a foul in the area. Louis Munteanu stepped up with composure, firing the penalty home to secure his second goal of the night and double the advantage. With a two-goal cushion, the visitors began to manage the clock, replacing their star man Munteanu with Jacob Murrell to provide fresh energy in the defensive phase. Late Resistance and Closing Discipline The final fifteen minutes were a stop-start affair as the referee worked hard to maintain control over a fraying contest. Nicolas Fernandez Mercau entered the book for the hosts in the 80th minute, followed by several tactical substitutions as NYCFC threw on Jonathan Shore and Seymour Reid in a desperate attempt to salvage a result. However, the organized DC United backline refused to buckle under the late pressure. In a lengthy period of stoppage time, Jacob Murrell picked up a yellow card for a cynical foul, but it did little to dampen the spirits of the traveling side. When the referee eventually blew the final whistle after ten minutes of added time, DC United had successfully navigated a difficult away trip to claim all three points. It was a professional performance that highlighted their clinical edge in front of goal and their ability to thrive in a high-pressure sports environment.

matches.description: Watch DC United vs CF Montreal highlights and goals from Major League Soccer on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 24, 2026. The MLS season delivered one of its most chaotic encounters yet as the sun set on a high-stakes clash. With momentum swinging violently from side to side, both teams pushed their physical and tactical limits until the final seconds. Early Dominance at Audi Field On 2026-05-24 , D.C. United took to the pitch with an aggressive stance, looking to dictate the tempo from the opening whistle. Their pressure paid dividends as early as the 9th minute when Louis Munteanu found the back of the net to open the scoring. The home side's dominance continued to grow, and in the 28th minute, Jared Stroud doubled the lead, leaving CF Montréal reeling within the first half-hour. The visitors' frustration was evident as Olger Escobar picked up a yellow card shortly after. However, CF Montréal found a lifeline deep into first-half stoppage time. In the 45+1 minute, Prince Osei Owusu displayed his clinical edge to pull a goal back, turning what looked like a D.C. United monologue into a competitive contest heading into the break. A Seesaw Battle in the Second Half The second half began with D.C. United attempting to re-establish total control. In the 51st minute, a penalty was awarded to the hosts, and Tai Baribo made no mistake from the spot to make it 3-1. But the Canadian response was swift; by the 61st minute, Prince Osei Owusu netted his second of the match following an assist from Wikelman Carmona , in a sequence that also saw yellow cards for Brandon Servania and Daniel Rios as the intensity flared. When Lucas Bartlett scored D.C. United ’s fourth goal in the 87th minute, assisted by Keisuke Kurokawa , victory seemed certain for the capital club. A 4-2 scoreline late in the game usually signals the end, but football had a dramatic script reserved for the dying moments. Stoppage Time Mayhem CF Montréal ’s resilience was tested and proven in a frantic finish. At 90+4', Prince Osei Owusu converted another penalty to complete his hat-trick and ignite hope. Just two minutes later, at 90+6', the unthinkable happened: substitute Gennadiy Synchuk equalized after being set up by the omnipresent Owusu . Tempers boiled over in the final moments, with a flurry of yellow cards issued to Victor Loturi , Lucas Bartlett , Matthew Longstaff , and Owusu himself. The final whistle at 90+14' brought an end to an epic 4-4 draw, a match defined by late drama and an incredible refusal to lose by the visitors.
